clue.text: Late worker, near to start of week, left

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: the start of the word week supplies its opening letter only

explanation.surface: Someone describes a night-shift worker who knocks off early in the week.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma pieces read in order: NIGH, TO, the W that starts 'week', and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who stays up working into the small hours is called by the name of a nocturnal bird.

clue.text: Drama on island involving a famous boat

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece comes before the next
involving means surrounding, so the drama takes the letter in

parts.note: Noh is a classical form of Japanese drama
Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A play staged on an island featuring a celebrated vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: NOH involves A, giving NOAH; 'on' sets it above SARK, one of the Channel Islands, off France.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch built a great vessel to survive the Flood, the most celebrated boat of all.

clue.text: Very clear setter's enveloped in a good deal of elegance

indicators.note: enveloped in means wrapped inside another piece
a good deal of means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: grace means elegance of movement or manner
the setter of this puzzle is Phi, and setter's stands for setter is

explanation.surface: The compiler claims to be wrapped in plenty of style.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi is the setter of this puzzle, so 'setter's' gives his pseudonym; 'a good deal of' drops the last letter and 'enveloped in' puts the pseudonym inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A graphic description is vividly detailed, so clear it paints a picture.

clue.text: Two learners in part of Austria

parts.note: a tyro is a novice or learner
L is the learner-driver plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A pair of novices find themselves somewhere in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: The two learners are given in two ways: TYRO, a novice, and L, from the learner-driver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine province in western Austria.

clue.text: Someone determined to root out bad spelling?

definitions.text: Someone determined to root out bad spelling?

parts.words: Someone determined to root out bad spelling?
parts.note: spelling read not as orthography but as casting spells, and the person hunts down those who cast evil ones

explanation.surface: A stern teacher out to eradicate poor orthography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad spelling' looks like poor orthography but means evil spell-casting.
explanation.definitionFit: In the seventeenth century an official was paid to hunt out practitioners of sorcery.

clue.text: Give one representative skill

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand over a single delegate's talent.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart knowledge is to give or pass it on to someone.

clue.text: Notes wrongly made about nasty Roman

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece surrounds the other
wrongly means the letters of the word made are set down in the wrong order
nasty signals that the letters of Roman are messed up

explanation.surface: Someone has written unkind memos about an unpleasant Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' makes MEDA and 'nasty' makes MORAN; 'about' sets the first around the second. 'nasty Roman' reads as a description but is fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda are written notes or reminders, the Latin plural of memorandum.

clue.text: Give life to article on one seaman

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mate is a ship's officer, a seaman

explanation.surface: Bring to life a story about one sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate something is to bring it to life or make it move.

clue.text: Chap's in exam, not finishing the papers

indicators.note: in means placed inside the test word
not finishing means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a test is an exam
chap's means he is, contracted to he's

explanation.surface: A man in an exam fails to complete the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' cuts TEST to TES; HE'S goes 'in' it: T(HES)ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Theses are dissertations, academic papers presented for a degree.

clue.text: Readiness to have a bet about review

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to lay is to place a bet
a crit is a short informal word for a critical review

explanation.surface: Someone eager enough to wager on how a critic's notice will turn out.
explanation.walkthrough: To lay a bet is a bookmaker's term; 'about' puts the review inside the bet, after a plain A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity is eager promptness, a readiness to act at once.

clue.text: Power held by Eastern prince with Eastern realm

indicators.note: held by means the first piece is gripped inside the prince

parts.note: an emir is a Muslim prince or ruler in the Middle East
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A tale of an oriental ruler grasping authority over his eastern kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a large domain ruled by one sovereign, a kind of realm.

clue.text: It's a hot place, mostly

parts.note: describes a sun-baked semi-arid strip of land that is largely hot and dry

explanation.surface: A remark about somewhere that tends to be warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The semi-arid belt along the southern edge of the Sahara is described in plain terms; 'mostly' hedges because it is a fringe zone rather than full desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahel is the semi-arid region of Africa bordering the Sahara, mostly very hot.

clue.text: Stay out in the cold?

parts.note: read not as being excluded but as remaining dormant through the winter months, as some animals do

explanation.surface: Someone is left excluded from a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay out in the cold' sounds like being left out socially; here it means sitting out the cold season asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals such as bears and hedgehogs spend winter in a dormant state to survive the cold.

clue.text: Staff offering shock ENGL treatment?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Staff offering shock ENGL treatment? (7,4)': 'ENGL' is OCR garble with no scan or reprint to restore the original wording.

clue.text: Opposition cancel erratic rallies

indicators.note: rallies as in regroups or reassembles, so the letters are brought together in a new order

explanation.surface: Political opponents rally against an unpredictable cancellation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erratic' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'rallies' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalcitrance is stubborn resistance to authority, a form of opposition.

clue.text: Image shows lake polluted with oil? That's about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go around the next piece
polluted means fouled or spoilt, so the letters of the words are jumbled

parts.note: OK means right or correct

explanation.surface: A picture of a lake contaminated with oil, confirmed as accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polluted' turns the seven letters of the lake and oil into LOALIKE, and 'That's about' wraps that around the word for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookalike is a double, someone who is the image of another.

clue.text: Family member's gory story?

definitions.meaning: a kinsman by birth, someone related to you through descent; the 's stands for 'is'
a relation is also a telling or account, so a bloody one is a gruesome tale

explanation.surface: A relative turns out to be a horror tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'relation' in its sense of a narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman by descent shares your ancestry; read literally, the phrase is a gruesome narrative.

clue.text: Airman almost ran riot

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: colours that ran have bled
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aviator nearly went on the rampage.
explanation.walkthrough: Dyes that run in the wash are said to bleed, so 'ran' is a past tense of that verb; 'almost' cuts its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Blériot was the French aviator who first flew across the English Channel in 1909.

clue.text: I am very keen about Old Norse period of history

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the second piece is placed inside

parts.note: to rage is to be fervently passionate, as in all the rage

explanation.surface: Someone confesses passion for the Vikings' language and era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the Old Norse abbreviation inside the rage, after I; 'am very keen' is fair because to rage about something can mean to be wildly enthusiastic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age is the prehistoric period when iron tools came into use.

clue.text: Plan not to retain jewel in the in rock layers

indicators.note: not to retain means the named item is let go from the word

parts.note: a stratagem is a scheme or plan
a gem is a jewel

explanation.surface: A scheme that will not hold on to a precious stone found among rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to retain' strips GEM from STRATAGEM; 'in the in' is a garbled link.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers of sedimentary rock lying one on another.

clue.text: Ruth uses a curious wordbook

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the letters before it are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth consults an odd dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book listing words grouped by synonyms.

clue.text: Post Office impounding sexy picture

indicators.note: impounding means seizing and holding, so the first piece is wrapped around the second

parts.note: hot means sexy or attractive

explanation.surface: Postal authorities confiscate a racy image.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a photograph, a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Jab King in card game

parts.note: to poke is to jab
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Prod the monarch while playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a gambling card game of bluff and betting.

clue.text: Sharp account about former dictator

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda in the 1970s
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A biting report on a deposed tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: IDI is Idi Amin, the crossword's stock dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic taste or remarks are sour, biting, tart.

clue.text: Reserve shown by chap (one between the sheets)

parts.note: to book is to reserve
Mark is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A booking made by a man who seems to have a bedfellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between the sheets' suggests bed, but the sheets are the pages of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmark is a strip placed between the pages of a book to keep your place.

clue.text: Soldier has edge in song

parts.note: a soldier ant is a caste of ant, so ant stands for soldier
a hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: A fighting man with an advantage breaks into song.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a rousing song, such as a national hymn.

clue.text: Indication of support? Try and try again

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court
the same legal sense of trying a case, heard a second time

explanation.surface: A determined motto: keep trying until you succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is in the courtroom sense: a judge hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting the phrase twice in Parliament signals agreement with a speaker.
